content.comment_body: Hello experts, I'm working on a small project requiring around 15 I/O, with 1 analog input and 1 analog output. I am considering using [product_name] this time, along with a [product_name] HMI panel. Could someone advise on the latest [product_name] CPU and software to choose? Also, is the software available for free, or does it require purchasing a license? Additionally, I would appreciate information on whether the [product_name] CPU has a single or double Ethernet port, its user program memory, the model with the highest number of onboard I/O, and the maximum number of expansion modules supported. Thanks in advance. Regards,

There are several questions here which can't be answered in brief. The current [product_name] CPU can support: Digital inputs: 24 Digital outputs: 20 Analog inputs: 8 Analog outputs: 8 A [product_name] base module typically includes 8 digital inputs and 4 digital outputs. Depending on your selection, you can have models offering 4 analog inputs and 4 fast counter inputs. For example, using 2 analog inputs and 2 fast counter inputs limits you to 4 standard inputs. Base modules feature only one Ethernet port. Digital expansion modules are provided in two main variants: - One with 4 digital inputs and 4 digital outputs - Another with 8 digital inputs and 8 digital outputs Note that digital expansion modules lack analog and fast counter inputs. Analog input modules offer two analog inputs, selectable between voltage and current ranges. Analog output modules feature two outputs, also selectable between voltage and current ranges. There are also specialized analog modules for temperature measurement. Edit: Programming software for [product_name] requires purchasing a single license. Similarly, programming software for the HMI panel also needs a license. The Starter Kit bundles both softwares included for [product_name] and the respective HMI.
The attached [document] is an excerpt from the current manual, which shows how to configure the maximum I/O setup for a [product_name] base module.
Hello [user_name], Thank you for sharing the details. I have one more question: Is it possible to use the HMI panels [product_name] or [product_name] with the [product_name] PLC? Regards,

Both panels can be used. The choice between Basic and Comfort Panel determines which software you need. For a Basic Panel, WinCC Basic is adequate. For a Comfort Panel, WinCC Comfort is needed, which is more expensive.

Yes [user_name], I've previously used TIA Portal and Basic panels with [product_name], but I'm not sure about the configuration or settings required for communicating with [product_name] panels and a [product_name] PLC. Regards,
[company_name] offers a website with practical application examples. There are examples that cover communication between [product_name] and WinCC.
Thank you very much. The provided information is genuinely useful. Regards,
A new question posted by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread with the subject 'Require 1 AI & 1 AO [product_name] PLC'. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users unfamiliar with the [product_name] ecosystem often have questions about software licensing, hardware specifications, and compatibility with HMI devices. There's a noticeable demand for clear and accessible documentation outlining hardware limitations, software requirements for both PLC and HMI programming, as well as distinctions between product versions. New users may have difficulty finding consolidated information related to I/O capacity, Ethernet port details, memory size, and licensing needs, which can complicate initial setup and integration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate thorough advice on available [product_name] hardware and software, including transparent details about licensing, and direct statements about compatibility with HMI panels. They seek clear guidance on integration to streamline their setup process.
